subject: ISV gateway: technical reference implementation and lead-tiering
messages:
From: Nathan Brooks <nathan.brooks@orionanalytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orion Analytics Partnerships <partners@orionanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SOW + revenue mechanics for gateway integration

Irene — thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a first-pass SOW and a proposed revenue-share table for the ISV gateway integration we discussed (see IA-Gateway-Integration-SOW-draft.pdf). High level: Orion will route customers through a lightweight gateway adaptor for the first 90 days, then expand to the full SDK integration.

Primary asks from our side:
- Clear lead-registration steps and protection windows (how long is a lead protected once registered).
- Exact rev-share % for gateway vs SDK-enabled opportunities (we proposed a 20/35 split in the draft).
- Who owns the implementation and support escalation matrix for the canary period.

We'd like to move quickly — can your partnerships and sales-ops teams confirm the commercial ops and a short acceptance/QA checklist for the gateway approach?

Attachments: IA-Gateway-Integration-SOW-draft.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Nathan Brooks
Head of Partnerships, Orion Analytics
Nathan.Brooks@orionanalytics.com
+1 415 555 0123

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Nathan Brooks <nathan.brooks@orionanalytics.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SOW + revenue mechanics for gateway integration

Nathan — appreciate the draft and the clear summary. Looping in Camila (partnerships) and Ben (sales ops) to validate the commercial flow and lead-protection mechanics.

Quick proposed next steps:
1) Camila to confirm lead-tiering/protection and commission schedule (Ben to confirm routing and HubSpot workflow).
2) Marissa (integration PM) will be pulled into a technical design sync for the gateway adaptor — we prefer a short canary before full SDK.
3) We'll aim to return an edited SOW with tracked changes and an acceptance checklist by EOD Friday.

Can you confirm your legal team is comfortable with our standard partner addendum? If so we can include it as an appendix to the SOW.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Nathan Brooks <nathan.brooks@orionanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SOW + revenue mechanics for gateway integration

Thanks Nathan — I reviewed the draft and attached a focused lead-tiering table (lead-tiering-table.csv) with our recommended protection windows and commission breakpoints. Key points:
- Lead registration: partner must register in HubSpot with source param + onboarding form. Registration window: 14 days to claim inbound demo request; protection period: 12 months for registered leads.
- Commission tiers: Gateway (first 90d): 18% rev-share; SDK-enabled conversions (post full integration): 30% rev-share.
- Onboarding credit: one-time $2k engineering credit for gateway canary for implementation support (deducted from first payout).
- Clawback: 6 months for refunds/cancellations on ARR-based deals.

Requested from Redwood Legal: add explicit language that lead registration must include (a) HubSpot ID, (b) signed mutual action plan or qualifying notes, and (c) evidence of engagement (call recording/meeting notes).

Ben — can you confirm tracking + payout cadence? Nathan — if Orion needs a longer protection window for specific named accounts, we can review case-by-case.

-Camila
Camila Reyes
Director, Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Nathan Brooks <nathan.brooks@orionanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SOW + revenue mechanics for gateway integration

Thanks all — quick ops notes from Sales Ops:
- HubSpot: we'll create a Partner-Registration form and a workflow (HS-OR-134) that stamps the partner ID and TTL on the contact record. That will drive ROI reports and payout eligibility.
- Payout cadence: quarterly, net-30 after invoice. We recommend an initial holdback equal to the onboarding credit until first payment settles.
- Rev recognition: for gateway-led deals where Redwood invoices, revenue will be recognized normally; payout to Orion is computed on realized revenue after refunds/credits.

Technical suggestion (ops-friendly): start with the gateway adaptor for low-friction onboarding. If the canary proves metrics (activation, retention) then move to an SDK flow and increase rev-share per Camila's tiers. This protects both sides during the early phase.

Attachment: ops-implementation-notes.docx (stub)

Action items I will own: HubSpot workflow, payout mapping, and updating partner dashboard. ETA: draft workflows by Thu 4/1.

-Ben Carter
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Nathan Brooks <nathan.brooks@orionanalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SOW + revenue mechanics for gateway integration

Ben / Camila / Irene — good plan. We support the canary -> SDK ramp. Attached is a redline of the SOW with two asks we need explicitly called out: (1) the rev-share table as fixed percentages for the first 12 months post-activation, and (2) the lead-protection onboarding workflow (HubSpot form + confirmation email) used to validate registrations.

Regards,
Nathan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nathan Brooks <nathan.brooks@orionanalytics.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SOW + revenue mechanics for gateway integration

Nathan — thanks for the redline. From an implementation and QA standpoint here are the acceptance criteria and runbook items we'll include in the SOW appendix:
1) Canary success metrics (30-day activation >= 45%, 90-day retention >= 20%).
2) Error-rate SLA for gateway adaptor (p95 latency < 350ms, error rate < 1%).
3) Logging and tracing: gateway must forward request IDs and include a minimal event schema for conversion attribution.
4) Escalation matrix for support (first-level Orion, second-level Redwood on-call + priority bugfix SLA during canary).
5) Delivery milestones: gateway adaptor code drop (T+3 weeks), canary start (T+5 weeks), SDK plan review (T+9 weeks).

I'll update the SOW appendix to include these items and merge the commercial table Camila provided. Camila/Ben/Irene — I'll circulate a tracked version by EOD today for legal to review.

-Marissa Cole
Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference

(Attachment note: will attach the updated SOW appendix and runbook when circulating.)
